```{r setup, include=FALSE}

#--------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run first if not already installed
#--------------------------------------------------------------------

#remotes::install_github("pbs-assess/sdmTMBextra", dependencies = TRUE)
#remotes::install_github("pbs-assess/sdmTMB", dependencies = TRUE)

#--------------------------------------------------------------------
# If sdmTMBextra fails because of INLA install, use the following:
#--------------------------------------------------------------------

#remotes::install_version("INLA", version = "25.06.13",
#repos = c(getOption("repos"), INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/testing"), dep = TRUE) 

#--------------------------------------------------------------------
# Begin setup
#--------------------------------------------------------------------

rm(list=ls())
gc()

load.lib <- c("tidyverse", "data.table", "cowplot", "sf", 
              "here", "sdmTMB", "sdmTMBextra", "rnaturalearth",
              "rnaturalearthhires", 
              "mregions2" # Pulls official maritime EEZ records from MarineRegions.org
              ) 

install.lib <- load.lib[!load.lib %in% installed.packages()]

for(lib in install.lib) install.packages(lib,dependencies=TRUE)
sapply(load.lib,require,character=TRUE)

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

dir <- here(getwd())

source(here(dir, "functions.R"))

```

# Regroup data 2 Seasons

There is moderate to strong temporal autocorrelation in the model as the modelling mean absolute error is significantly reduced by inclusion of temporal effects. However the spatial effects are not be well captured.

## Save unfiltered years for future analyses 

```{r, allyears.future.analyses}

AllYears.dat <- full.dat2 |>
  mutate(YearSeas = paste(year(date), Season, sep = "")) |>
  mutate(Season.nm = 
           case_when(
             grepl("Spring", Season) ~ 1,
             grepl("Summer", Season) ~ 2
             ),
         # Combine year and numeric season
         YearSeas.nm = (Year + (Season.nm - 1) / 10))

# Note this will be on row per standard length
fwrite(AllYears.dat,
       here(dir, "Data",
            "AllYears.Unfiltered.Canada.and.CPS.ATM.Survey.Data.csv"),
       sep = ",")

```

## For model runs by season (excluding spatiotemporal footprint mismatch)

These are the years where you will actually run the model.

```{r, 2season.structure}

TwoSeas.dat <- full.dat2 |>
  # Remove fall entries and years where there is low data
  filter(Season != "Fall" & !Year %in% c(2001:2007, 2009:2011)) |>
  mutate(YearSeas = paste(year(date), Season, sep = "")) |>
  # Remove summer hauls where they only sampled in north
  #filter(!YearSeas %in% c("2004Summer", "2005Summer", "2006Summer")) |>
  mutate(Season.nm = 
           case_when(
             grepl("Spring", Season) ~ 1,
             grepl("Summer", Season) ~ 2
             ),
         # Combine year and numeric season
         YearSeas.nm = (Year + (Season.nm - 1) / 10))
# View(TwoSeas.dat)  

unique(TwoSeas.dat$YearSeas)
unique(TwoSeas.dat$YearSeas.nm)

test <- full.dat2 |> filter(Year == 2025)
unique(test$Country)
# [1] "USA"

```

### Find Missing Seasons

```{r, missing.seasons}

# Generate complete sequence
# Define the range of years
years <- 2008:2025

# Create the sequence of year-season combinations
year_season_sequence <- data.frame(
  YearSeas.nm = unlist(lapply(years, function(year) {
  # For each year, create two entries: season 1 (0.0) and season 2 (0.1)
  ## year + 0/10 gives 2003.0,while year + 1/10 gives 2003.1
  c(year + 0 / 10, year + 1 / 10)  
}))
)

# Print the resulting sequence
year_season_sequence

missing_seas <- year_season_sequence |>
  anti_join(TwoSeas.dat, by = "YearSeas.nm") |>
  select(YearSeas.nm)

missing_seas

```

```{r, filter.and.save.missing.years}
# Define all levels for Year Quarter, combining training data and extra_time (numeric)
all_levels2 <- sort(unique(c(TwoSeas.dat$YearSeas.nm, missing_seas$YearSeas.nm)))

# Define extra time steps to estimate
```

# Convert to transect data

```{r, create.spatial.object}

TwoSeas.dat.st <- TwoSeas.dat |>
  group_by(keys) |>
  mutate(FID = keys) |>
  make_transect_sf(crs = 4326) |>
  ungroup()

# Since the data falls within two UTM zones and there is not an ideal projection to use, apply a custom equal area albers projection
aea_custom <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=30 +lat_2=50 +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-124.5 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

# Project to Albers Equal Area Conical
TwoSeas.dat.st.aea <- TwoSeas.dat.st |>
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom) 

# Extract polygon centers
TwoSeas.dat2 <- TwoSeas.dat.st.aea |>
  # Extract the centre of the transect (this is in km)
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(geometry))[,1]/1000,
         Y = st_coordinates(st_centroid(geometry))[,2]/1000) |>
  st_drop_geometry() 

# View(TwoSeas.dat)
fwrite(TwoSeas.dat2, here(dir, "Data",  "Canada.and.CPS.ATM.Survey.Data.csv"))

range(TwoSeas.dat2$X)
# [1] -548.3906  946.8199

range(TwoSeas.dat2$Y)
# [1] -1219.072  1623.044

```

## Construct the Seasonal Mesh: 

### Load coastline

```{r, load.coastal.geometries}

# 1. Direct GitHub URL for the Shapefile ZIP
url <- "https://github.com/GenericMappingTools/gshhg-gmt/releases/download/2.3.7/gshhg-shp-2.3.7.zip"

# 2. Set up temporary file paths
zip_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
ex_dir <- tempdir()

# 3. Download the archive (mode = "wb" prevents binary corruption on Windows)
download.file(url, destfile = zip_path, mode = "wb")

# 4. Unzip
unzip(zip_path, exdir = ex_dir)

# 5. Read into R with 'sf'
# Resolutions: 'f' (full), 'h' (high), 'i' (intermediate), 'l' (low), 'c' (crude)
shp_path <- file.path(ex_dir, "GSHHS_shp", "f", "GSHHS_f_L1.shp")
coastline <- st_read(shp_path)

# 6. Verify plot
plot(st_geometry(coastline))

# 7. Define boundaries - previously derived from the full us data 
# (all seasons and years 2003 to 2024) with 100 m buffer around transects
## Note that this was done on an older data set that is no longer available so will be updated in the next
## iteration
bbox_vec <- c(xmin = -581615.7, ymin = -1218974.1, xmax = 949523.9, ymax = 1634799.5)

# 7. Crop to study area
coastline.clip <- coastline |>
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(aea_custom)) |>
  ### Trim to area extent
  st_crop(bbox_vec)

```

### Create Barrier Mesh

```{r, construct.barrier.mesh}

# Filter the data frame
TwoSeas.dat_filtered <- 
  TwoSeas.dat2[TwoSeas.dat2$X >= min(TwoSeas.dat2$X) & 
                 TwoSeas.dat2$X <= max(TwoSeas.dat2$X) & 
                 TwoSeas.dat2$Y >= min(TwoSeas.dat2$Y) & 
                 TwoSeas.dat2$Y <= max(TwoSeas.dat2$Y), ]

# Cutoff values control the minimum distance between knots.
## It is generally better to start with a coarser mesh (larger cutoff)
## However there is a tradeoff on spatial predictability (more knots) and
## over fitting the time to process. If the day is irregularly distributed
## you can also try residual-based knot placement
meshTwoSeas.dat_filtered <- make_mesh(TwoSeas.dat_filtered, 
                                       xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), 
                                       cutoff = 20) 

# Check number of mesh nodes 
## If greater than >1,000–2,000 nodes, 
## you’re likely in trouble unless you have a lot of RAM.
length(meshTwoSeas.dat_filtered$mesh$loc[,1])
# [1] 594

plot(meshTwoSeas.dat_filtered)
points(TwoSeas.dat_filtered$X, TwoSeas.dat_filtered$Y, col = "red", pch = 19, 
       cex = 0.2) 

# proj_scaling should match units of (since we are working in m, but density
# is in km, divide by 1000)
barrier2 <- sdmTMBextra::add_barrier_mesh(meshTwoSeas.dat_filtered, coastline.clip, proj_scaling = 1000)

## If greater than >1,000–2,000 nodes, 
## you’re likely in trouble unless you have a lot of RAM.
length(barrier2$mesh$loc[,1])
# [1] 594

# Example plot code from ?add_barrier_mesh
mesh_df_water2 <- barrier2$mesh_sf[barrier2$normal_triangles, ]
mesh_df_land2 <- barrier2$mesh_sf[barrier2$barrier_triangles, ]

Mesh.with.barrier2 <-
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = coastline.clip) +
  geom_sf(data = mesh_df_water2, size = 1, colour = "blue") +
  geom_sf(data = mesh_df_land2, size = 1, colour = "green")

Mesh.with.barrier2

plot(meshTwoSeas.dat_filtered)
points(TwoSeas.dat_filtered$X, TwoSeas.dat_filtered$Y, col = "red", pch = 19, 
       cex = 0.2) 

plot(st_geometry(coastline.clip))
```

Next, create boundaries

```{r, year.lat.bin.trend}

#------------------------------------------------------
# Create stock boundary limits
#------------------------------------------------------

# Create point sf 
limits <- data.frame(
  X = c(-124.06946, -120.47072),
  Y = c(40.02236, 34.44872)
  ) 

limits.sf <- st_as_sf(limits, coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom)

# Create northern stock boundary (Westernmost Point, CA)
nstock <- st_coordinates(limits.sf)[1,2]/1000

# Create southern stock boundary (Point Conception, CA)
point.concept <- st_coordinates(limits.sf)[2,2]/1000

#------------------------------------------------------
# Create upper and lower spatial domain limits
#------------------------------------------------------

hlines <- us_eez |>
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom) |>
  mutate(
    # Create southern US EEZ boundary
    ymin = st_bbox(geometry)["ymin"]/1000,
    # Create northern US EEZ boundary
    ymax = st_bbox(geometry)["ymax"]/1000
    ) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(ymin, ymax)

#------------------------------------------------------
# subset by latitudinal bin and sum over year, season, and country
#------------------------------------------------------

TwoSeas.dat_filtered <- 
  TwoSeas.dat_filtered |>
    mutate(latBin = 
             case_when(
               Y < unique(hlines$ymin) ~ "BajaCa",
               Y >= unique(hlines$ymin) & 
                 Y < point.concept ~ "SCaBaj",
               Y >= point.concept & 
                 Y < nstock ~ "Califo",
               Y >= nstock &
                 Y < unique(hlines$ymax) ~ "PNWUSA",
               Y >= unique(hlines$ymax) ~ "Canada"
               )
           ) 

#------------------------------------------------------
# Summarise the data
#------------------------------------------------------

TwoSeas.dat_filtered.latitude.test <- TwoSeas.dat_filtered |>
  filter(scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax") |>
  group_by(Year, Season, latBin, keys) |>
  summarise(Haul.kg = sum(Scaled_Biomass_Contribution), .groups = "keep") |>
  ungroup()


TwoSeas.dat_filtered.latitude <- TwoSeas.dat_filtered |>
  filter(scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax") |>
  group_by(Year, Season, latBin) |>
  summarise(Haul.kg = sum(Scaled_Biomass_Contribution), .groups = "keep") |>
  ungroup()

#------------------------------------------------------
# Plot output
#------------------------------------------------------

trend.check3 <-
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = TwoSeas.dat_filtered.latitude |> 
              filter(Season == "Summer"),
            aes(x = Year, y = Haul.kg/1000, col = latBin)) +
  # Force a linear trend so they don't wiggle ridiculously
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(data = TwoSeas.dat_filtered.latitude.test |> 
               filter(Season == "Summer"),
             aes(x = Year, y = Haul.kg/1000, col = latBin, group = keys)) +
  facet_wrap(~latBin) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 20) +
  ylab("Metric tons (mt)") +
  xlab("Year")

trend.check3

#------------------------------------------------------
# Save output  
#------------------------------------------------------

ggsave2(filename="S2.trend.check.by.latBin.w.integrated.Canadian.dat.wght.only.jpeg",
        plot=trend.check3, device="jpeg", 
        path=here(dir, "Final.Figures"), dpi=1200, width = 29, height=21, 
        unit="cm", limitsize = FALSE)
```

## Regroup latBin based on density patterns

Here "BajaCa", "ScaBaj", "Califo" are all very similar and can probably be grouped together.

```{r, regroup.southern.boundaries}

#------------------------------------------------------
# For like boundary areas
#------------------------------------------------------

TwoSeas.dat_filtered.south <- 
  TwoSeas.dat_filtered |>
  filter(latBin %in% c("BajaCa", "ScaBaj", "Califo")
         ) |>
  # Group BajaCa, ScaBaj, and Califo
  mutate(latBin = "SofMendocino",
         Present = 
           case_when(
             scientific_name != "Sardinops sagax" ~ 0,
             scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax" ~ 1
           )
         )

#------------------------------------------------------
# For remaining boundary areas
#------------------------------------------------------

TwoSeas.dat_filtered.north <- 
  TwoSeas.dat_filtered |>
  filter(!latBin %in% c("BajaCa", "ScaBaj", "Califo")
         ) |>
  # Group BajaCa, ScaBaj, and Califo
  mutate(Present = 
           case_when(
             scientific_name != "Sardinops sagax" ~ 0,
             scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax" ~ 1
           )
         )

#------------------------------------------------------
# Join everything back together
#------------------------------------------------------

TwoSeas.dat_filtered.Binned <- rbind(TwoSeas.dat_filtered.south,
                                      TwoSeas.dat_filtered.north)

#------------------------------------------------------
# Double check that no rows were lost
#------------------------------------------------------

dim(TwoSeas.dat)
# [1] 24223    24

dim(TwoSeas.dat_filtered.Binned)
# [1] 24223    29

unique(is.na(TwoSeas.dat_filtered.Binned))

fwrite(TwoSeas.dat_filtered.Binned, 
       here(dir, "Data", "Canada.and.CPS.ATM.Survey.Data.w.latBin.csv"))

```

# Create summary table

```{r}

# 1. Prepare Spatial and Temporal Features
TwoSeas.2008_2019.sf <- TwoSeas.dat_filtered.Binned |> 
  filter(Season == "Summer" & Year %in% c(2008, 2012:2019)) |>
  make_transect_sf(crs = 4326) |>
  mutate(latBin = 
           case_when(
             latBin %in% c("BajaCa", "SCaBaj", "Califo") ~ "SofMendocino",  # Fixed 'SCaBaj'
             latBin == "PNWUSA" ~ "PNWUSA",
             latBin == "Canada" ~ "Canada",
             TRUE ~ latBin  # Safety line to preserve any unmatched values rather than turning them into NA
             ),
         len.bin = 
           case_when(
             len.bin == "less150" ~ "<15.0", 
             len.bin == "150to200" ~ "15.0-20.0", 
             len.bin == "200+" ~ "20.0+"
             )
  )
  
unique(TwoSeas.2008_2019.sf$latBin)
# [1] "SofMendocino"  "PNWUSA"  "Canada"  

TwoSeas.2008_2019_prep.sf <- TwoSeas.2008_2019.sf |>
  separate(date, into = c("Year_num", "Month", "Day"), remove = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    Year = as.numeric(Year_num),
    Month_num = as.numeric(Month),
    Month_abb = month.abb[Month_num],
    MonthDay_str = paste0(Month_abb, ". ", Day),
    MonthDay_idx = as.numeric(paste0(Month, Day)),
    CountryLatBin = paste(Country, " - ", latBin)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, CountryLatBin, keys) |> 
  mutate(
    # Extract the lowest latitude from the transect key
    minLAT = min(st_coordinates(geometry)[, "Y"]),
    # Extract the greatest latitude from the transect key
    maxLAT = max(st_coordinates(geometry)[, "Y"])
    ) |>
  ungroup() 


# 2. Build Consolidated Summary Table
TwoSeas.2008_2019survey.dat <- TwoSeas.2008_2019_prep.sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(Year, CountryLatBin) |>
  summarise(
    # Temporal range per bin
    MonthDay = paste(
      MonthDay_str[which.min(MonthDay_idx)], 
      "-", 
      MonthDay_str[which.max(MonthDay_idx)]
    ),
    
    # Latitudinal range per bin
    Latitudes = paste0(
      format(round(min(minLAT, na.rm = TRUE), 2), nsmall = 2), 
      " - ", 
      format(round(max(maxLAT, na.rm = TRUE), 2), nsmall = 2)
    ),
    
    # Haul Counts
    `Total Hauls` = n_distinct(keys),
    `Nb. Absent Hauls` = n_distinct(keys[scientific_name == "Other" | is.na(len.bin)]),
    
    # Catch & Biological Metrics (without duplication by haul key)
    `Total Catch (kg)` = sum(
      Species_weight[!duplicated(keys) & scientific_name != "Other" & !is.na(len.bin)], 
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    `n sampled` = sum(
      lenBin.nb[!duplicated(keys) & scientific_name != "Other" & !is.na(len.bin)], 
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    `Length Bins (cm)` = {
      # Clean out NAs, empty strings, and white spaces
      clean_bins <- len.bin[scientific_name != "Other" & !is.na(len.bin) & trimws(len.bin) != ""]
      
      if (length(clean_bins) == 0) {
        "None"
        } else {
          # Define custom level order
          bin_order <- c("<15.0", "15.0-20.0", "20.0+")
          
          # Convert to factor with explicit order and sort
          ordered_bins <- sort(factor(unique(clean_bins), levels = bin_order))
          
          # Collapse into string
          paste(ordered_bins, collapse = " & ")
          }
      }
    ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    Year, MonthDay, `Country - Strata` = CountryLatBin, `Total Hauls`, `Nb. Absent Hauls`,
    `Total Catch (kg)`, `Length Bins (cm)`, `n sampled`, Latitudes
    )

View(TwoSeas.2008_2019survey.dat)

# 3. Save Output
fwrite(TwoSeas.2008_2019survey.dat, here("Final.Results", "SummerSummaryTable.csv"))

# Calculate dataset-wide summary statistics
overall_stats <- TwoSeas.2008_2019survey.dat |>
  summarise(
    Total_Hauls       = sum(`Total Hauls`),
    Absent_Hauls      = sum(`Nb. Absent Hauls`),
    Present_Hauls     = sum(`Total Hauls`) - sum(`Nb. Absent Hauls`),
    Percent_Zeros     = round((sum(`Nb. Absent Hauls`) / sum(`Total Hauls`)) * 100, 2),
    Total_Fish_Sampled= sum(`n sampled`),
    Total_Catch_kg    = sum(`Total Catch (kg)`),
    Mean_Catch_kg     = round(mean(`Total Catch (kg)`[`Total Catch (kg)` > 0]), 2),
    Median_Catch_kg   = round(median(`Total Catch (kg)`[`Total Catch (kg)` > 0]), 2),
    Min_Catch_kg      = round(min(`Total Catch (kg)`[`Total Catch (kg)` > 0]), 2),
    Max_Catch_kg      = round(max(`Total Catch (kg)`), 2)
  )

View(overall_stats)

```
```{r}

# 1. Prepare Spatial and Temporal Features (with safer date indexing)
TwoSeas.2008_2019_prep.sf <- TwoSeas.2008_2019.sf |>
  mutate(
    date_parsed = as.Date(date),
    Year = as.numeric(format(date_parsed, "%Y")),
    Month_abb = format(date_parsed, "%b"),
    Day = format(date_parsed, "%d"),
    MonthDay_str = paste0(Month_abb, ". ", Day),
    MonthDay_idx = lubridate::yday(date_parsed), # Chronological day of year (1-366)
    CountryLatBin = paste(Country, " - ", latBin)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, CountryLatBin, keys) |> 
  mutate(
    minLAT = min(st_coordinates(geometry)[, "Y"]),
    maxLAT = max(st_coordinates(geometry)[, "Y"])
  ) |>
  ungroup()


# 2. Build Consolidated Summary Table
TwoSeas.2008_2019survey.dat <- TwoSeas.2008_2019_prep.sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(Year, CountryLatBin) |>
  summarise(
    # Temporal range per bin
    MonthDay = paste(
      MonthDay_str[which.min(MonthDay_idx)], 
      "-", 
      MonthDay_str[which.max(MonthDay_idx)]
    ),
    
    # Latitudinal range per bin
    Latitudes = paste0(
      format(round(min(minLAT, na.rm = TRUE), 2), nsmall = 2), 
      " - ", 
      format(round(max(maxLAT, na.rm = TRUE), 2), nsmall = 2)
    ),
    
    # Haul Counts
    `Total Hauls` = n_distinct(keys),
    `Nb. Absent Hauls` = n_distinct(keys[scientific_name == "Other" | is.na(len.bin)]),
    
    # Total Catch Weight: Filter valid target rows first, then take 1 weight per distinct key
    `Total Catch (kg)` = {
      valid_target <- scientific_name != "Other" & !is.na(len.bin)
      target_keys <- keys[valid_target]
      target_weights <- Species_weight[valid_target]
      sum(target_weights[!duplicated(target_keys)], na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    
    # Fish Sampled Count: Sum ALL length bin counts for target species (do NOT deduplicate keys)
    `n sampled` = sum(
      lenBin.nb[scientific_name != "Other" & !is.na(len.bin)], 
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    # Length Bins
    `Length Bins (cm)` = {
      clean_bins <- len.bin[scientific_name != "Other" & !is.na(len.bin) & trimws(len.bin) != ""]
      
      if (length(clean_bins) == 0) {
        "None"
      } else {
        bin_order <- c("<15.0", "15.0-20.0", "20.0+")
        ordered_bins <- sort(factor(unique(clean_bins), levels = bin_order))
        paste(ordered_bins, collapse = " & ")
      }
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  select(
    Year, MonthDay, `Country - Strata` = CountryLatBin, `Total Hauls`, `Nb. Absent Hauls`,
    `Total Catch (kg)`, `Length Bins (cm)`, `n sampled`, Latitudes
  )

View(TwoSeas.2008_2019survey.dat)

```
